messages.content: What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?

function.name: locate_tallest_mountains
function.description: Find the tallest mountains within a specified radius of a location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city from which to calculate distance.

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

function.name: calculate_genotype_frequency
function.description: Calculate the frequency of homozygous dominant genotype based on the allele frequency using Hardy Weinberg Principle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

allele_frequency.description: The frequency of the dominant allele in the population. This is a float type value.

genotype.description: The genotype which frequency is needed, default is homozygous dominant.

function.name: cellbio_get_proteins
function.description: Get the list of proteins in a specific cell compartment. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

include_description.description: Set true if you want a brief description of each protein.

message.content:
**Proteins that are typically found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Function | Representative Examples | |----------|----------|------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often form channels, carriers, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (carrier)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors** (e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, muscarinic acetylcholine receptor)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** (e.g., EGFR, HER2)
• **Ion channels** (e.g., voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv1.2, calcium channel Cav1.2)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions. | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane stability)
• **Band‑3 protein** (anion exchanger in red blood cells)
• **Protein kinase C** (binds to phospholipids)
• **Glycophorin A** (red‑cell membrane protein, peripheral) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and reside on the outer leaflet. | • **CD59** (protectin, GPI‑anchored)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored)
• **Thy-1** (GPI‑anchored) | | **Extracellular matrix‑binding proteins** | Interact with the extracellular matrix or other cells. | • **Fibronectin** (integrin ligand)
• **Collagen‑binding integrins** (α2β1) | | **Signal‑transduction proteins** | Transmit signals across the membrane. | • **Src family kinases** (associate with membrane via lipid modifications)
• **Phosphatidylinositol 3‑kinase (PI3K)** (membrane‑associated) | ### How to use this list - **Research**: If you’re studying a particular cell type, you can filter the list by the proteins most relevant to that tissue (e.g., GLUT4 in adipose tissue, CFTR in epithelial cells). - **Experimental design**: Knowing whether a protein is integral or peripheral helps decide on detergent solubilization strategies for membrane isolation. - **Bioinformatics**: Many databases (UniProt, Gene Ontology) annotate proteins with “plasma membrane” as a cellular component; you can cross‑reference the above examples to retrieve detailed functional data. Feel free to ask for more specific subsets (e.g., “what are the plasma‑membrane receptors in neurons?”) or for additional details on any of the proteins listed.
